plain_text:
MANCHESTER SCHOOL DISTRICT SAU #37 
SPECIAL COMMITTEE ON ATHLETICS 
 
September 9, 2026 9:00 a.m.  
 
1. Chairwoman Stewart called the meeting to order at 9:30 a.m. 
 
2. The Clerk called the roll.  
 
 Present: Committee Member Stewart, Parr and Garrity. 
 Absent: Committee Member O’Connell and Bergeron. 
 
 
3. Public Forum 
 
There was no one present wishing to give comment. 
 
 
6. Approval of the Minutes of the following meetings: June 10, 2026. 
 
On motion of Committee Member Parr, duly seconded by Committee Member Garrity, it was moved to 
approve the minutes of the June 10th, 2026 meeting.  Motion passed. 
  
 
7. PRESENTATIONS  
 
There were no presentations. 
 
 
8. Policy Review – Students 521: Expectations for Students in Athletics with Academic  
Expectations Procedures; Students 539: Student Insurance; and, Students 542: Student  
Physical Examinations – by Dr. Kelly Espinola, Assistant Superintendent 
 
Dr. Espinola introduced three policies that the Athletics Committee will review and bring forward with 
recommendations in the coming months: 
 Policy 521 – Expectations for Students in Athletics/Academic Expectations 
 Policy 539 – Student Insurance 
 Policy 542 – Student Physical Examinations 
 
Dr. Espinola explained that Policy 539 had not been reviewed since 2001 and previously referenced a 
low-cost student insurance option that is no longer available. Policy 521 was last reviewed in 2023 and 
incorporates academic eligibility expectations connected to NHIAA requirements. Policy 542 addresses
September 9, 2026 Special Committee on Athletics

student physical examinations and includes language concerning the District's responsibility for physical 
examinations. 
 
The Committee discussed the need to review the three policies together to ensure that eligibility 
requirements, insurance provisions, physical examination requirements, and related District policies are 
consistent. 
 
Student Insurance and Liability 
The Committee discussed the former availability of low-cost student insurance through Gerber 
Insurance. Attorney Upton explained that Gerber no longer provides the individual policy previously 
available to families. The District currently purchases supplemental coverage at approximately $11,000 
annually that may provide coverage above a student's existing health insurance in certain circumstances. 
It was noted that current District policy continues to require health insurance even though the former 
low-cost option referenced in the policy is no longer available. Families without health insurance are 
provided information regarding Healthy Kids and other available resources. 
 
Attorney Upton explained that the presence or absence of health insurance does not necessarily change 
the District's underlying liability; rather, insurance provides a source for payment of medical expenses 
and may reduce the likelihood of claims being brought against the District. 
 
The Committee discussed whether students without health insurance should be able to participate 
through a more comprehensive liability waiver. Attorney Upton stated that waivers are most effective 
when they clearly and specifically describe the risks being assumed. The existing athletic registration 
waiver is brief and may need to be revised as part of the larger policy review. Ms. Telge and Mr. 
D’Onofrio confirmed that parents currently sign a waiver through the athletics registration portal for 
each season and attest that their student has health insurance. 
 
The Committee also discussed whether similar waiver and insurance considerations should apply to 
other student activities, including marching band, performing groups, clubs, and other extracurricular 
activities. 
 
The Administration emphasized the importance of cross-referencing related policies during the review 
process so that District policies do not conflict with one another.
September 9, 2026 Special Committee on Athletics 
Page 3 of 7 
 
 
Attorney Upton will review the existing waiver and enrollment forms and develop possible revisions. He 
will also contact Kevin O'Neill to attend a future meeting and provide additional information regarding 
the District's self-insured status, existing supplemental coverage, and potential insurance options. 
 
Student Physical Examinations 
A significant portion of the discussion focused on Policy 542 and the number of student-athletes who 
currently have either no physical examination on file or an outdated physical. 
Ms. Telge and Mr. D’Onofrio reported the following fall athletics information: 
 
West High School 
 149 rostered athletes 
 49 students with no physical on file 
 85 students with an outdated physical 
Central High School 
 240 rostered athletes 
 14 students with no physical on file 
 57 students with an outdated physical 
Memorial High School 
 241 rostered athletes 
 161 students with no physical on file 
 50 students with an outdated physical 
 
Ms. Telge and Mr. D’Onofrio explained that athletic trainers generally use approximately a 14-month 
timeframe when identifying physical examinations as outdated and work with students and families to 
provide reminders before their physical expires. 
 
The Committee discussed the possibility of moving from an annual physical examination requirement to 
a physical every two years. Ms. Telge and Mr. D’Onofrio reported that many New Hampshire school 
districts currently use a two-year requirement for student-athletes. 
 
The Administration will also obtain information regarding the physical examination requirements for the 
general student population and research practices in other school districts.
September 9, 2026 Special Committee on Athletics 
Page 4 of 7 
 
 
The Committee expressed concern regarding students participating in athletics without a physical 
examination on file. Attorney Upton noted that physical examinations provide an important screening 
tool for health conditions, including congenital conditions that could create additional risks during 
athletic participation. 
 
Access to Affordable Physicals 
Ms. Telge and Mr. D’Onofrio discussed ongoing efforts to provide free or low-cost physical 
examinations to students.  The District partnered with the National Guard during the summer to provide 
free physical examinations. This program is supported through a federal Innovative Readiness Training 
(IRT) initiative. The District must apply annually, with paperwork due by September 30.  The National 
Guard hopes to provide physical examinations twice annually, potentially once during the winter and 
again during the spring or summer, depending upon provider availability. 
 
Ms. Telge and Mr. D’Onofrio explained that previous efforts to partner with community providers were 
complicated by students and families scheduling free appointments and then failing to attend, resulting 
in lost appointment time for providers.  They continues extensive outreach to families through athletic 
trainers, coaches, emails, telephone calls, and direct communication with students. Staff also provide 
information regarding available low-cost physical examination options. 
 
The demand for free physicals remains significant. When the District offered free appointments through 
the National Guard, available appointments filled within approximately 40 minutes and approximately 
80 students were placed on a waiting list. Staff continued contacting families throughout the event to fill 
appointments that became available because of cancellations or no-shows. 
 
The Committee discussed bringing providers directly into District schools rather than requiring families 
to travel to outside locations. Ms. Telge and Mr. D’Onofrio confirmed that physical examinations can be 
conducted in school nursing offices when qualified providers are available. 
 
Potential Fund for Student Physicals 
The Committee discussed establishing a community-supported fund to assist families for whom the cost 
of a physical examination is a barrier.  Potential contributors discussed included alumni athletes, local 
businesses, banks, healthcare providers, and other community partners.
September 9, 2026 Special Committee on Athletics 
Page 5 of 7 
 
Ms. Telge and Mr. D’Onofrio indicated that a basic sports physical may cost approximately $25 to $40 
depending on the provider. Based on the current number of fall athletes lacking appropriate physical 
documentation, an initial estimate of approximately $10,000 was discussed for fall athletics alone. 
Administration noted that a more complete estimate should also consider students participating in 
intramural sports, clubs, marching band, and other activities potentially covered by revised policies. 
 
The Committee discussed the possibility of using a voucher system administered through school nurses 
or athletic trainers so that eligible families could receive assistance directly. 
 
Elliot Health System was identified as an existing community partner involved with the National Guard 
physical examination initiative, and the Committee discussed exploring whether healthcare partners 
might assist with reduced-cost physicals in conjunction with a community-supported fund. 
 
The Committee generally supported further exploration of community partnerships and alumni 
engagement rather than reallocating existing athletics funds, which could require reductions elsewhere 
in the athletics budget. 
 
Policy Review Next Steps 
The Administration will continue reviewing Policies 521, 539, and 542 and will: 
 Research practices and physical examination requirements in other New Hampshire school 
districts; 
 Review District data regarding physical examinations for the broader student population; 
 Explore moving toward a two-year physical examination requirement; 
 Examine potential revisions to student and parent waiver forms; 
 Review insurance and liability options with the District's insurance/risk management 
representatives; 
 Explore community partnerships and potential funding sources for low-cost or free physical 
examinations; 
 Consider how revised requirements may apply to athletics, extracurricular activities, performing 
groups, clubs, and other student programs; and 
 Ensure related District policies are cross-referenced and aligned.
September 9, 2026 Special Committee on Athletics 
Page 6 of 7 
 
The Committee acknowledged that its immediate focus is athletics but noted that recommendations 
developed through this process may ultimately have broader implications and could be referred to the 
Policy Committee for additional review. 
 
No action was taken on the policy items at this meeting. 
 
9. Upcoming Items: 
 
a. Alumni Athletes 
b. The roll and identification of Community Partners. 
 
 
10. NEW BUSINESS  
 
Fall Athletics Update 
Ms. Telge and Mr. D’Onofrio provided an update on fall athletics.  At the high school level, all 
anticipated teams are being fielded.   
1. Football participation remains strong across the three high schools. Central High School 
increased from 38 football players last year to 52 this year and is operating both a varsity team 
and a freshman/reserve schedule. 
2. Boys soccer participation remains strong throughout the District. Central experienced increased 
participation and was able to maintain three strong rosters and add freshman games to its 
schedule. 
3. Girls soccer numbers remain generally consistent with recent years. Central and West continue to 
operate a cooperative girls soccer program. Four West students currently participate in the 
cooperative program, with two playing varsity and two playing junior varsity. Due to the limited 
West participation numbers, the cooperative arrangement will continue. The District will monitor 
participation again next year to determine whether separate Central and West teams may 
eventually be viable.  Memorial experienced a modest increase in girls soccer participation. 
4. Volleyball participation remains strong at all three high schools. 
5. Cross country participation is down, particularly among boys. Girls participation remains 
generally consistent with recent years, with some variation among the individual schools. 
6. Golf participation is also down. Memorial currently has seven golfers and Central has four. 
7. At the middle school level, gameplay was beginning at the time of the meeting.  
a. Boys soccer participation remains strong across the District.
September 9, 2026 Special Committee on Athletics 
Page 7 of 7 
 
b. Girls soccer numbers are lower at most middle schools, with Southside being the 
exception.  
c. Volleyball continues to have strong participation at all four middle schools.  
d. Cross country participation is down across the city, consistent with the trend seen at the 
high school level. 
 
ADJOURNMENT 
 
 
11. If there is no further business, a motion is in order to adjourn.  
 
 
On motion of Committee Member Garrity, duly seconded by Committee Member Parr, it was moved to 
adjourn.  All were in favor, meeting adjourned at 9:50 a.m.
